newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says magnate paid taxes, but too late.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says magnate paid taxes, but too late.

text.p: Mexican authorities on Monday said cellular phone magnate Carlos Peralta had fully paid the back taxes he owed, but too late to avoid the issuing of an arrest warrant against him on charges of tax fraud.
Peralta, meanwhile, blamed an "administrative error" for the late payment, and denied he had committed any crime. He said a Mexico City judge had suspended the arrest warrant on Monday.
"The error was of an administrative nature, in no moment was there fiscal fraud. On Jan. 31 of this year (the debts) were paid, and no crime was committed," he told reporters.

On Sunday, the Finance Ministry and the Attorney General's Office announced that an arrest warrant had been issued against Peralta, a member of one of Mexico's richest families, alleging he had bilked the taxman of some $5 million.
The Finance Ministry has launched a crackdown on tax evaders, targeting some high-profile suspects.

Peralta caused a scandal last year when he acknowledged he had once lent $50 million to ex-president Carlos Salinas' brother Raul, who is in jail on murder and illicit enrichment charges, without asking for a receipt.

Some radio commentators on Monday suggested that payment may have earned him the wrath of the government, though the Finance Ministry has avidly denied it is engaged in any sort of "fiscal terrorism" against its adversaries.

On Monday, the authorities acknowledged Peralta had made the payment, but said the fact he paid up did not free him from penal action. It alleged the taxes were withheld between 1992 and 1995, and said it was up to a judge to decide what sanction should be handed out.

Until recently, Peralta was vice-chairman of Grupo Iusacell, one of Mexico's two main cellular phone companies, in which his family owns the largest stake. U.S. phone company Bell Atlantic Corp owns 42 percent.

Last month, Mexican authorities gave the go-ahead to Bell Atlantic to assume management control of Iusacell, freeing Bell -- not necessarily deliberately -- from any potential headaches from the government's action against Peralta.
The Peralta family was ranked by Forbes among the country's top billionaires last year, and owns holding company Grupo Iusa.
